The `empty`, `hello`, `matches`, and `entropy` fixtures were generated with Zstandard CLI v1.5.7 (`zstd -q -3 --check --stream-size=<decoded length> -c`), with `-5` for the entropy vector, reading the exact `decoded` bytes on stdin. These committed `encoded` bytes include seed-zero XXH64 checksums. No encoder or subprocess runs in the test suite. `empty` independently exercises the published XXH64 empty-input value `ef46db3751d8e999` (low 32-bit trailer `99 e9 d8 51`). Raw and RLE framing cases are constructed directly from RFC 8878 sections 3.1.1 and 3.1.1.2.

Source: https://github.com/facebook/zstd/tree/v1.5.7 and https://github.com/Cyan4973/xxHash/blob/v0.8.3/tests/sanity_test_vectors.h .

`direct-weights-compressed-sequence-tables` uses a block from `zstd -q -9 --no-check -c`, placed in an RFC single-segment frame with its known 4096-byte content size and independently revalidated with `zstd -q -d -c`: four Huffman streams with direct weights, predefined literal-length table and FSE-compressed offset/match-length tables. Its 4096-byte, eight-symbol source is pinned alongside the encoded frame.

`rle-sequence-and-treeless` and `repeat-sequence-and-treeless` were generated with libzstd v1.5.7 `ZSTD_compressStream2`, compression level 9, flushing after the first two of three input segments and ending after the third. Segment sizes are respectively 512 and 1024 bytes. Their non-single-segment window descriptor is reduced to 64 KiB, then each complete frame is independently decoded with `zstd -q -d -c` and compared to its pinned output. The first covers an RLE match-length table; the second covers a repeated match-length table. Both reuse Huffman tables through treeless literal blocks.

`rle-literals` and `one-stream` are tiny RFC constructions independently cross-validated with `zstd -q -d -c`. The first has an RLE literal section and zero sequences (output `AAA`). The second has a direct two-symbol Huffman tree and one reverse bitstream (output `[1, 0]` four times). These prove distinct literal modes without larger input matrices.
